research_gaps.description: Australian sites and cultures require place-specific excavation chronologies and Indigenous permissions; no single continent-wide medieval political entity.
Beyond Kongo founding, Central African societies and settlement archaeology need dedicated research.
Mali, Ife, Benin, Mossi and Kanem early dynastic dates often rest on mixed oral, epigraphic and later records.
Amazonian and Orinoco historical societies remain much more weakly represented than highland Andean states.
Taino and Kalinago societies deserve specialist pre-1492 archaeological and linguistic treatment.
Mississippian, Southwest and Plains traditions must be expanded with local archaeological cultures and contemporary descendant perspectives.
Older UNESCO and Met descriptions suggest very early remote-island settlement; recent archaeological reassessments often place it later; do not flatten differences.
Kangnido and al-Idrisi original compositions and later copies/facsimiles must not share one object date.
Reproduction rights for individual cartographic facsimiles and artworks have not been cleared.
No individually validated time-sliced territorial polygons; modern reference anchors are not political extents.
Regional plague mortality and ecological causes need specialist source triangulation.
Many state foundation/end dates are simplified conventional markers; refine into time-dependent episodes.
Gunpowder, compass and print technology diffusion paths require independent corroboration; parallel appearance is not direct transmission.
Medicine education and care in African, American and Pacific societies need specialist research.
Medieval mills clockwork and mechanical systems were under-sampled in this pack.
Direct port-to-port journeys versus indirect commodity chains need tighter site and text sourcing.
Census-like population figures should not be inserted without estimate methods, ranges, sources and uncertainties.
Women children non-elite workers enslaved people and ordinary food and housing practices remain underrepresented.
Historical-language names and scripts are incomplete; sources sometimes use colonially mediated or retroactive labels.
Most draft records have regional orientation sources only; more independent claim-level review before publication.
Overlapping 500-999 and 1000-1499 entities must keep stable IDs and one canonical record; technology comparisons require status merging.
Ming, Joseon, Ottomans, Inca and Aztec processes continue beyond 1499, and future batch should not fabricate a collapse.
